phases.name: Set the release contract and source boundary
phases.description: Separate stated release constraints from assumptions, then connect the source repository to Azure Pipelines and its build workers.

phases.name: Build once and enforce verification gates
phases.description: Run parallel automated tests, coverage and code-quality checks, image security scanning, container publishing, and reviewed Terraform plans.

phases.name: Promote the same release through environments
phases.description: Separate CI from controlled deployment promotion and roll one immutable image through development, staging, and production AKS targets.

phases.name: Switch traffic safely, observe, and recover
phases.description: Keep blue serving while green is validated, gate traffic changes on health, record approvals and deployment history, and retain a fast rollback path.

steps.phase: Set the release contract and source boundary
steps.title: Separate the brief from sizing assumptions
steps.content: The brief requires automated build and tests, multiple environments, blue-green deployment, IaC, performance monitoring, rollback, and code-quality gates. Its stated constraints are deployment under 10 minutes, zero downtime, automated-test coverage greater than 80%, multistage approvals, and maintained deployment history. It does not define repository size, test-suite duration, application traffic, latency SLOs, or environment topology; measure these instead of inventing capacity claims.

steps.phase: Set the release contract and source boundary
steps.title: Define what the 10-minute target measures
steps.content: The brief states a deployment-time target under ten minutes, but does not define the clock boundary. Record queue time, automated build and verification, rollout, and each approval wait separately; do not silently stop the clock before a required approval. Confirm the start and end events with stakeholders, then assess the under-ten-minute target against that definition. Until then, do not claim end-to-end compliance.

decision.question: How should the under-10-minute deployment target coexist with multistage manual approvals?
decision.chosen: Keep the stated under-ten-minute deployment target, record automated execution and approval wait separately, and confirm the clock boundary before claiming the target is met.
decision.chosenReason: This preserves the brief's target without assuming that multistage approval wait is excluded from deployment time.

alternatives.option: Count only the final AKS rollout
alternatives.tradeoff: Hides slow builds, tests, or quality gates that users experience as part of delivery.
Makes the end-to-end target misleading and cannot be guaranteed by pipeline automation.

steps.phase: Set the release contract and source boundary
steps.title: Add the source repository
steps.content: Use the existing GitHub catalog component as the source-repository example and connect it to Azure Pipelines. This is an explicit source-host assumption because the brief names Azure Pipelines but does not require Azure Repos; replacing the Git host changes the trigger integration, not the release gates.

component.label: Application Source Repository

properties.purpose: Store application source, versioned pipeline YAML, test definitions, and Terraform modules. Protect the main branch with reviewed pull requests and required passing status checks; do not store deployment secrets in repository files.

component.highlightReason: GitHub is already a supported version-control component; the problem allows GitHub and does not mandate Azure Repos.

steps.phase: Set the release contract and source boundary
steps.title: Add Azure Pipelines as the CI orchestrator
steps.content: The existing CI/CD Pipeline component directly supports Azure DevOps. Use pull-request validation and a main-branch run after merge; make the stage order explicit so image publication and environment promotion cannot bypass test or quality failures.

component.label: Azure Pipelines — CI
component.description: PR validation, build orchestration, and release handoff

properties.purpose: Run PR validation and post-merge CI. Order stages as checkout -> parallel build/test/quality/security -> publish one immutable image digest -> hand off to controlled CD. Fail closed on any required gate; use federated workload identity rather than long-lived cloud credentials.
properties.stages: checkout -> build -> parallel tests/quality/security -> publish immutable image -> promote

component.highlightReason: The catalog CI/CD Pipeline exposes Azure DevOps as a supported platform and models the requested automation.

steps.phase: Set the release contract and source boundary
steps.title: Trigger validation from reviewed source changes
steps.content: A pull request starts validation against the proposed commit; a merge to the protected branch starts the release candidate run. Record the exact commit SHA so later deployment and rollback history can be traced to source.

connection.label: PR + protected-branch events
connection.description: Source commit and review state trigger Azure Pipelines validation

steps.phase: Set the release contract and source boundary
steps.title: Add isolated build workers
steps.content: Use the existing Build Server type for Azure Pipelines agents. Prefer ephemeral or isolated workers, parallel jobs, and dependency/build caches; never let an untrusted pull-request job reuse production deployment credentials.

component.label: Azure Pipelines Build Agents
component.description: Parallel, isolated application and image builds

properties.purpose: Build the application and OCI image on isolated hosted agents. Enable dependency and layer caching, parallelize independent jobs, pin toolchains, and publish timing by stage. Treat the job count as a tunable setting, not a workload-derived capacity promise.

component.highlightReason: Build Server is the existing palette component for automated compilation and image-build workers.

steps.phase: Set the release contract and source boundary
steps.title: Dispatch the pipeline jobs to build agents
steps.content: Azure Pipelines schedules the build and verification jobs on the worker pool. Use parallelism for independent suites, but preserve required gates: a faster run must not skip tests or lower the agreed coverage threshold.

connection.label: Build + verification jobs
connection.description: Pipeline schedules isolated, cache-aware build workers

steps.phase: Set the release contract and source boundary
steps.title: Build once and promote the same image digest
steps.content: Do not rebuild an image separately for development, staging, and production. Build once from the reviewed commit, identify it by immutable digest, and promote that exact artifact after each environment gate. This makes production rollback and deployment history refer to a verifiable artifact rather than a mutable tag.

decision.question: Should each environment rebuild the container or promote one tested artifact?
decision.chosen: Build one image after required gates, store its immutable digest, and promote the same digest through every environment.
decision.chosenReason: The artifact that passed tests is the artifact deployed, and the digest provides a stable rollback and audit identity.

alternatives.tradeoff: Different bytes can reach production even when source revisions appear identical.
A tag can move, so history may not identify the exact image that ran.

steps.phase: Build once and enforce verification gates
steps.title: Add automated test suites and a strict coverage threshold
steps.content: Use the existing Automated Testing component for unit, integration, end-to-end, and selected performance tests. The requirement is strictly greater than 80%, so configure an 81% minimum rather than accepting 80%; publish the coverage report and fail the pipeline when the threshold or required suite fails. Azure Test Plans can hold test cases and traceability while the pipeline executes the automated suites.

component.label: Azure Test Plans + Automated Suites
component.description: Parallel tests with an enforced coverage floor

properties.componentName: Azure Test Plans + CI Test Suites
properties.purpose: Run unit, integration, API-contract, and release smoke tests in parallel; map test cases to requirements in Azure Test Plans. Publish coverage per commit and block promotion below 81% so the stated >80% constraint is met.

component.highlightReason: Automated Testing is an existing DevOps component with explicit test-type, parallel-execution, and coverage-threshold properties.

steps.phase: Build once and enforce verification gates
steps.title: Run tests and collect coverage from the build
steps.content: The build job supplies the tested revision and artifacts to the suite. Preserve test results and coverage as pipeline artifacts so reviewers can see which commit passed and why a gate blocked promotion.

connection.label: Parallel tests + coverage report
connection.description: Automated suites validate the built revision and publish coverage

steps.phase: Build once and enforce verification gates
steps.title: Add a blocking code-quality gate
steps.content: Use the existing Code Quality component for lint, static analysis, and maintainability policy. A failed gate must stop artifact publication or environment promotion; make thresholds visible rather than treating a green build as proof of quality.

component.label: Code Quality Gate
component.description: Static analysis and merge-blocking quality rules

properties.purpose: Run static analysis and lint on the changed revision; block merge or release on failed quality-gate rules, new blocker/critical findings, or coverage below the pipeline threshold. Preserve the report with the build record.
properties.thresholds: Coverage >=81%; no new blocker/critical quality findings

component.highlightReason: Code Quality is a native catalog type that exposes tools, quality-gate enablement, and thresholds.

steps.phase: Build once and enforce verification gates
steps.title: Make quality results a release input
steps.content: Run the quality checks against the same commit that produced the test report and image candidate. A failed static-analysis gate cannot be waived by a successful deployment approval.

connection.label: Lint + static-analysis report
connection.description: Quality checks evaluate the exact release-candidate revision

steps.phase: Build once and enforce verification gates
steps.title: Scan the candidate container before release
steps.content: Use the existing Security Scanning component for a container-image scan. Pin scanner rules and fail on high-severity vulnerabilities; document any approved exception with an owner and expiry instead of silently allowing a vulnerable image through.

component.label: Container Image Security Scan
component.description: Trivy scan blocks vulnerable image promotion

properties.purpose: Scan the built container and its dependencies before publication/promotion. Fail on high-severity findings; attach the scan report and any time-bounded, approved exception to the commit and image digest.

component.highlightReason: Security Scanning is a supported DevOps palette component with a native Container scan type and Trivy option.

steps.phase: Build once and enforce verification gates
steps.title: Block release on a failed image scan
steps.content: The build produces an image candidate for scanning. A clean scan is a required gate before that image digest becomes eligible for environment promotion; keep the scan result associated with the digest in the release record.

connection.label: Candidate image + scan policy
connection.description: Trivy evaluates the built image before it is released

steps.phase: Build once and enforce verification gates
steps.title: Use Azure Container Registry for immutable images
steps.content: The Docker catalog component has an explicit ACR registry option, so use it for image build/publish rather than creating an unsupported registry node. Push only after required tests and scans pass, tag with the commit for discoverability, and promote by digest rather than tag.

component.label: Azure Container Registry (ACR)
component.description: Private store for the verified OCI release image

properties.purpose: Store the verified OCI image with immutable digest identity, restricted push/pull roles, retention for supported rollback, and vulnerability-scan metadata. AKS obtains pull access through managed identity; do not embed registry passwords in manifests.

component.highlightReason: Docker is an existing catalog component whose registry property explicitly supports ACR and Kubernetes orchestration.

steps.phase: Build once and enforce verification gates
steps.title: Publish only the gate-approved image
steps.content: After tests, quality checks, and image scanning pass, publish the image digest to ACR. The pipeline stage ordering is the enforcement mechanism; do not treat this connection as permission to publish before gates complete.

connection.label: Gate-approved image digest
connection.description: Only a candidate that passed required checks is stored for promotion

steps.phase: Build once and enforce verification gates
steps.title: Add versioned infrastructure definitions
steps.content: Infrastructure as Code is already modeled in the DevOps palette. Use Terraform modules for AKS, ACR, identities, network policy, and monitoring configuration; plan on pull requests and apply only through the gated environment stages.

component.label: Terraform Infrastructure

properties.purpose: Version AKS, ACR, managed identities, network controls, and monitoring resources as reusable modules. Produce a reviewable plan on pull requests; apply a saved, approved plan with least-privilege workload identity and environment-specific inputs.

component.highlightReason: Infrastructure as Code is an existing palette component with Terraform and Azure Blob state options.

steps.phase: Build once and enforce verification gates
steps.title: Plan infrastructure changes from the pipeline
steps.content: Azure Pipelines runs Terraform validation and plan from the versioned source. Keep remote state in Azure Blob with access control and locking; require review of destructive or unexpected changes before any environment apply.

connection.label: Validate + review Terraform plan
connection.description: Infrastructure plans are versioned, reviewed, and applied by gated stages

steps.phase: Build once and enforce verification gates
steps.title: Choose one IaC tool and make state durable
steps.content: The catalog also supports ARM Templates, but this walkthrough chooses Terraform rather than mixing deployment tools. Store remote state in Azure Blob, protect it with least-privilege access and state locking, and promote reviewed plans through the same approval boundaries as application releases.

decision.question: How should Azure infrastructure be defined and state managed?
decision.chosen: Use reusable Terraform modules with an Azure Blob remote backend and locking; apply an approved saved plan per environment.
decision.chosenReason: One versioned toolchain gives reviewable plans and consistent promotion while keeping state durable and access-controlled.

alternatives.tradeoff: A valid Azure-native choice, but mixing it with Terraform here would split plan and state workflows.
State is difficult to share safely across agents and can be lost with an ephemeral worker.

steps.phase: Build once and enforce verification gates
steps.title: Protect the time budget without weakening gates
steps.content: Measure queue time, each automated stage, rollout, and approval waits against the agreed deployment-time clock. Use hosted capacity, cached dependencies and image layers, parallel independent tests, and bounded timeouts to approach the stated under-10-minute target. If the full required path cannot meet the budget, optimize the stages and approval workflow or revisit feasibility with stakeholders; do not skip required tests or accept coverage at 80% to manufacture a green result.

steps.phase: Promote the same release through environments
steps.title: Add a separate deployment-promotion workflow
steps.content: Use the existing Deployment Pipeline component for environment progression, distinct from CI job execution. Define development, staging, and production as ordered stages; stage and production use approvals and health checks, while every stage deploys the same ACR digest.

component.label: Azure DevOps Environment Promotion
component.description: Ordered dev, staging, and production release stages

properties.purpose: Promote the same verified image digest and approved IaC plan through dev -> staging -> production. Use automatic health gates in dev, a staging verification/owner gate, and explicit production approval plus health checks. Record commit, digest, environment, approvers, gate outcomes, timestamps, and rollback outcome under the deployment-history retention policy.

component.highlightReason: Deployment Pipeline is an existing component with native Blue-Green strategy, environment, and rollback properties.

steps.phase: Promote the same release through environments
steps.title: Hand a completed CI run to controlled CD
steps.content: Only a CI run with passing required gates can create a promotion candidate. Carry its commit, test/quality/security evidence, immutable image digest, and approved infrastructure plan into the deployment workflow.

connection.label: Verified release candidate
connection.description: CI passes provenance and immutable artifact identity to CD

steps.phase: Promote the same release through environments
steps.title: Require automated-test evidence before promotion
steps.content: Test results and the coverage report are machine-checked by the release gate. A failed or missing suite, or coverage at or below 80%, blocks the candidate before it can enter an environment.

connection.label: Passing tests + coverage >80%
connection.description: Test and coverage evidence is required for environment promotion

steps.phase: Promote the same release through environments
steps.title: Require code-quality evidence before promotion
steps.content: A release approval cannot override a failed mandatory quality policy by itself. Any exception should use a separately authorized, auditable process with an owner and expiry.

connection.label: Required quality gate passed
connection.description: Code-quality status gates release eligibility

steps.phase: Promote the same release through environments
steps.title: Require a clean image-security result
steps.content: Only the image digest associated with a passing scan can be promoted. Persist the scan report and exception approvals alongside the release record so the gate is reproducible later.

connection.label: Approved image scan result
connection.description: High-severity findings block deployment of the candidate digest

steps.phase: Promote the same release through environments
steps.title: Apply only the reviewed infrastructure plan
steps.content: CD receives the exact saved Terraform plan that was reviewed. Re-plan and re-review if the source, state, or environment inputs change rather than applying stale infrastructure intent.

connection.label: Reviewed plan -> gated apply
connection.description: Environment infrastructure changes require an approved, current Terraform plan

steps.phase: Promote the same release through environments
steps.title: Resolve the immutable release from ACR
steps.content: CD pulls the image by digest and deploys that same artifact through every stage. Grant each AKS identity only the registry pull rights it needs; keep the digest and stage outcome in release history.

connection.label: Verified ACR image digest
connection.description: CD promotes the exact image that passed CI gates

steps.phase: Promote the same release through environments
steps.title: Add the development AKS target
steps.content: Use the existing Kubernetes component and choose AKS from its supported distribution options. Development is the first deployment target for integration and smoke validation; its exact size is not specified by the brief and must be selected from measured workload.

component.label: AKS — Development
component.description: First isolated environment for release-candidate checks

properties.purpose: Run the promoted image in an isolated development target; execute deployment smoke checks and validate configuration before staging. Size nodes and quotas from observed test workload rather than the catalog default.

component.highlightReason: Kubernetes is an existing component with AKS as a supported managed distribution.

steps.phase: Promote the same release through environments
steps.title: Deploy to development first
steps.content: The development stage deploys the immutable digest automatically after CI gates pass, then checks readiness and application smoke tests. A failed health check stops progression to staging.

connection.label: Auto deploy + smoke gate
connection.description: Development validation precedes promotion to staging

steps.phase: Promote the same release through environments
steps.title: Add the staging AKS target
steps.content: Represent staging separately from development so deployment configuration, test evidence, and approval context are environment-specific. Use production-like configuration and synthetic load without sharing production credentials or customer data.

component.label: AKS — Staging

properties.purpose: Run the same immutable image with production-like deployment settings; execute end-to-end, compatibility, and bounded performance smoke checks before production approval. Keep identities and secrets isolated from development and production.

component.highlightReason: The native Kubernetes component can represent a distinct AKS environment without inventing a provider-specific palette node.

steps.phase: Promote the same release through environments
steps.title: Promote only after staging checks pass
steps.content: After staging health, compatibility, and performance checks pass, require the designated staging owner approval before production becomes eligible. The manual approval wait is visible separately from automated execution time.

connection.label: Promote after dev + staging checks
connection.description: Staging results and owner approval are required before production

steps.phase: Promote the same release through environments
steps.title: Add the production AKS target
steps.content: Production is a separate AKS environment with stricter identity, network, quota, and change controls. Within it, keep the current blue deployment serving while a green deployment of the candidate digest starts and becomes ready; do not direct traffic to an unready revision.

component.label: AKS — Production (Blue + Green)
component.description: Production cluster with isolated blue and green workload slots

properties.purpose: Run separate blue and green Deployments/Services in production; blue continues serving while green is deployed, warmed, and checked. Use readiness probes, disruption budgets, least-privilege workload identities, and isolated environment configuration. Node count and topology remain workload-sizing decisions.

component.highlightReason: The existing managed Kubernetes component supports AKS; blue and green are workload slots within this production target, not invented node types.

steps.phase: Promote the same release through environments
steps.title: Deploy production only after its approval gate
steps.content: The production stage requires its authorized change approver and a successful staging record. It deploys the exact same digest into the green slot while blue remains healthy and routable.

connection.label: Approved digest -> green slot
connection.description: Production deployment starts only after multistage gates pass

steps.phase: Switch traffic safely, observe, and recover
steps.title: Use readiness-gated blue-green traffic switching
steps.content: Blue stays live while green starts and passes readiness, smoke, and compatibility checks. Shift production traffic only after green is healthy; retain blue through an agreed observation window. This avoids an in-place replacement gap, but zero downtime still depends on compatible schema changes, readiness behavior, and healthy capacity.

decision.question: When should production traffic move from blue to green?
decision.chosen: Keep blue serving, validate green with readiness and smoke checks, switch the stable service/ingress selector after the health gate, verify traffic convergence, and retain blue as the rollback candidate.
decision.chosenReason: The old version remains available until the candidate is proven ready. This supports the zero-downtime goal, but the actual result depends on readiness, capacity, compatibility, and traffic convergence.

alternatives.tradeoff: A bad rollout can remove the only healthy version before the candidate is ready.
A scheduled pod may not yet be ready or able to serve real requests.

steps.phase: Switch traffic safely, observe, and recover
steps.title: Add the production traffic switch
steps.content: Use the existing Layer 7 Load Balancer component to represent the stable ingress/service routing boundary in front of the production AKS workloads. The controller routes to the active healthy slot; do not expose a direct route to a candidate before approval and readiness checks pass.

component.label: AKS Ingress — Active Slot Router
component.description: Stable production endpoint for blue-green traffic changes

properties.purpose: Keep one stable production endpoint and route only to ready endpoints in the active blue or green slot. Change the selector after health gates pass and keep the previous healthy slot available for a selector rollback without rebuilding; measure routing convergence and recovery time.

component.highlightReason: Load Balancer is a supported Layer 7 component with health checks and traffic-routing properties; it represents the stable ingress boundary.

steps.phase: Switch traffic safely, observe, and recover
steps.title: Route production traffic to the active healthy slot
steps.content: The ingress boundary sends requests to the currently selected production Service. Readiness checks exclude unhealthy pods; after the controlled switch, the previous slot remains available until the observation policy permits cleanup.

connection.label: Stable endpoint -> ready blue/green slot
connection.description: Ingress directs traffic only to the selected healthy production deployment

steps.phase: Switch traffic safely, observe, and recover
steps.title: Add Azure performance and rollout monitoring
steps.content: Use the existing Monitoring component with Azure Monitor selected. Instrument both application performance and release health.

component.label: Azure Monitor + Application Insights

properties.purpose: Collect request rate, p95/p99 latency, error rate, saturation, pod readiness, probe failures, and release/version tags across environments. Compare green against blue during the observation window; alert and trigger rollback when approved SLO or health thresholds regress. Exclude secrets and sensitive payloads from telemetry. Set numeric SLO thresholds from product requirements and baseline measurements.

component.highlightReason: The existing Monitoring component now exposes Azure Monitor as a selectable stack.

steps.phase: Switch traffic safely, observe, and recover
steps.title: Observe production performance during the rollout
steps.content: Send production request and health signals to Azure Monitor with deployment-version tags. Compare the green candidate with the blue baseline during the observation window; a traffic switch is not considered successful merely because pods started.

connection.label: Latency, errors, saturation + readiness
connection.description: Production telemetry is segmented by active release version

steps.phase: Switch traffic safely, observe, and recover
steps.title: Observe development health and test outcomes
steps.content: Collect application request, latency, and error signals alongside deployment and test health from development so regressions are caught before staging. Keep environment labels on telemetry to prevent test traffic from being mistaken for production performance.

connection.label: Development health + smoke results
connection.description: Development signals are tagged separately from production

steps.phase: Switch traffic safely, observe, and recover
steps.title: Observe staging performance before approval
steps.content: Staging emits compatibility and bounded performance-test results with its environment identity. Make the staging owner review those results before approving production promotion.

connection.label: Staging latency + compatibility results
connection.description: Staging evidence is available to the production approval gate

steps.phase: Switch traffic safely, observe, and recover
steps.title: Record rollout timing and health against the release
steps.content: Azure Monitor correlates rollout events with application metrics. Emit stage start/end, automated execution duration, approval wait, health-gate outcome, active digest, and traffic-switch time so both the 10-minute target and approval workflow can be audited.

connection.label: Stage, approval + rollout events
connection.description: Release events are correlated with performance and health signals

steps.phase: Switch traffic safely, observe, and recover
steps.title: Use multistage approvals and durable deployment history
steps.content: Development can progress automatically after CI gates; staging requires its verification and owner check; production requires an authorized change approver after staging evidence. Keep approvers separate from the pipeline identity. For every stage, retain commit, image digest, IaC plan/run, approver, gate reports, timestamps, outcome, and rollback action under the organization’s audit retention policy.

decision.question: Where should human approvals and release history live?
decision.chosen: Use environment-scoped Azure DevOps checks at staging and production, with role separation, and retain run/deployment metadata and evidence according to the configured audit policy.
decision.chosenReason: Approvals become explicit stage gates and the history can identify who approved which exact source and artifact in each environment.

alternatives.option: One approval before the whole pipeline
alternatives.tradeoff: It does not provide distinct environment-level control or staging evidence review.

alternatives.option: Keep only the latest release record
alternatives.tradeoff: A rollback or incident investigation may lose the prior digest, approver, and gate evidence.

steps.phase: Switch traffic safely, observe, and recover
steps.title: Rollback by switching back to the last healthy digest
steps.content: If green fails before traffic moves, leave traffic on blue. If health regresses after the switch, initiate a selector rollback to blue, then verify that routing and application health recover before declaring rollback complete. Keep the previous image digest and compatible configuration available; treat database changes as backward-compatible expand/contract migrations so application rollback remains safe. Measure the recovery duration because the brief gives no rollback-time target.

decision.question: How does the system recover from a bad production release?
decision.chosen: Abort before traffic moves when green is unhealthy; after a regression, route back to the retained blue deployment and record the rollback against the failed release.
decision.chosenReason: A known previous version remains available, and its image digest identifies the recovery candidate.

alternatives.option: Rebuild the previous source revision during the incident
alternatives.tradeoff: Build delay and changed dependencies make the recovery artifact less predictable.
Removes the direct path to the previous version before the new version is proven stable.

steps.phase: Switch traffic safely, observe, and recover
steps.title: Review the end-to-end release contract
steps.content: The flow is source review -> Azure Pipelines build and parallel verification -> immutable ACR image -> reviewed Terraform and controlled CD -> dev -> staging -> approved production blue-green switch. Tests enforce coverage above 80%; Azure Monitor observes performance and rollout health; approvals and full deployment evidence are retained; an unhealthy release returns traffic to the previous digest. Validate the under-10-minute execution boundary and actual environment sizing with measured runs before claiming the target is met.
